chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar or Ibn Wahb, who said:
Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: For every salat (prayer) there are two times, and the beginning of the time is the better of the two.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُهُمَا: the better of the two, indicating greater merit
key_terms.أَوَّلُ: the beginning, referring to the earliest part of the prayer time
key_terms.وَقْتَانِ: two times, meaning two valid periods or ranges for performing the prayer

ai.seo_question: Is it better to perform salat (prayer) at the beginning of its time?
ai.summary: This hadith states that each salat (prayer) has two valid times within its appointed period. It emphasizes that performing the prayer at the beginning of its time is more excellent and preferable.
